scope.edit.widensNow: It takes effect at once; every administrator is told. You may be asked to confirm your identity.
scope.edit.widensPending: It goes back to pending and authorizes nothing until another approver approves it.
scope.entries.activateNeedsApprover: Activating widens scope: only a scope approver can do it.
scope.entries.emptyDescription: Scans refuse every internet target no entry covers.
scope.entries.extendNeedsApprover: A later expiry widens scope: only a scope approver can do it.

scope.entry.coverNameHint: Names below it stay out of scope.
scope.entry.coverSubHint: Pattern *.{name}. Add an exclusion of exactly the domain to leave it out.
scope.entry.descAdd: Say what your organization may probe. Exclusions still win over every entry.
scope.entry.descRequest: Ask a scope approver to allow one name or address for a few days. Scans may use it only after it is approved.
scope.entry.errKind: This is not a domain, IP address, IP range, URL, repository or cloud account. Pick its kind, or check the spelling.
scope.entry.errSave: Could not save the scope entry.
scope.entry.kindsHint: A domain, IP address, IP range, URL, repository or cloud account.
scope.entry.letterHint: The entry authorizes probes only while the letter is valid, and stops when it expires or is revoked.
scope.entry.noTierCeiling: An entry covers every probe: the scan intensity and the approval rules decide how hard its targets are scanned.
scope.entry.outcomeApproval1: Needs 1 approval from another approver; it authorizes nothing until then.
scope.entry.outcomeApprovalN: Needs {n} approvals from other approvers; it authorizes nothing until then.
scope.entry.outcomeNow: Takes effect at once. You may be asked to confirm your identity first.
scope.entry.outcomeRequest: A scope approver reviews it. It authorizes nothing until approved.
scope.entry.proofPlatform: Shared sensors also need proof that you control {domain}; your organization's sensors need this entry only.

scope.error.CIDR_TOO_LARGE: This address range is larger than the platform allows. Split it into smaller ranges.
scope.error.DENY_LIST: The platform does not allow this target as a scope entry.
scope.error.ENTRY_EXPIRED: This entry expired. Renew it with a new expiry instead.
scope.error.ENTRY_NOT_PENDING: This entry is not waiting for approval any more.
scope.error.ENTRY_REJECTED: This entry was rejected. Create a new one if it is still needed.
scope.error.ENTRY_SELF_APPROVAL: You requested this change, so another approver must approve it.
scope.error.EXCLUSION_REACHES_OUTSIDE_SC: This rule also matches assets you cannot see. Ask someone with access to them, or mark only the assets you see.
scope.error.INTRUSIVE_NEEDS_EXPIRY: Intrusive (T2) entries must expire in your organization (an owner may allow permanent ones) and need an approval.
scope.error.INTRUSIVE_TOO_LONG: An intrusive (T2) entry cannot last longer than your organization allows. An owner sets the limit in Scope settings.
scope.error.ONE_OFF_DISABLED: Your organization does not allow one-off scope entries.
scope.error.ONE_OFF_TOO_LONG: A one-off entry cannot last longer than your organization allows.
scope.error.PROOF_REQUIRED: These targets need a verified domain of your organization for this kind of scan. Verify the domain, or run the scan on your own sensor.
scope.error.PUBLIC_SUFFIX: A public suffix (such as com.vn or azurewebsites.net) cannot be a scope entry. Enter a domain your organization registered.
scope.error.REASON_REQUIRED: Say why this target may be probed. The reason is kept in the audit log.
scope.error.REMINDER_TOO_SOON: The approvers were reminded less than an hour ago.
scope.error.REQUEST_MUST_BE_ONE_OFF: A request must expire. Choose how many days it lasts.
scope.error.REQUEST_MUST_BE_SINGLE: A request covers one name or address. Wildcards and ranges need an approver.
scope.error.REQUEST_NOT_ALLOWED: Your organization does not accept scope requests from members.
scope.error.REQUEST_TIER: A request cannot ask for intrusive (T2) probes.
scope.error.SCOPE_ENTRY_EXISTS: Your organization already has this scope entry. Find it in the scope list instead of adding it again.
scope.error.SCOPE_EXCLUSION_EXISTS: Your organization already has this exclusion. Find it in the Out of scope list instead of adding it again.
scope.error.SCOPE_TARGET_TYPE_RETIRED: This type cannot be a scope entry. Add the domain, address or network that serves it.
scope.error.SCOPE_WILDCARD_NOT_ALLOWED: This kind of scope entry takes no wildcard. Name one exact value, or add a domain such as *.example.com.
scope.error.SELF_APPROVAL_INVALID_CODE: That code is wrong or was already used. Wait for your authenticator to show a new one.
scope.error.SELF_APPROVAL_NEEDS_TOTP: Approving your own entry needs a code from your authenticator app. Turn on two-factor authentication in your account first.
scope.error.SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED: You can approve your own entry only as an owner, and only when nobody else can approve it. Ask one of the approvers listed on the entry.
scope.error.SELF_APPROVAL_REASON_REQUIRE: Say why this entry may take effect without a second person. The reason is kept in the audit log.
scope.error.STEP_UP_REQUIRED: Confirm your identity to make this change.
scope.error.STEP_UP_UNAVAILABLE: This change needs you to confirm your identity, and your account has no way to do that here. Sign out and sign in again, then retry.
scope.error.TARGET_OUT_OF_SCOPE: Some targets may not be scanned. See each target for the reason.
scope.error.TARGET_SELECTOR_UNAVAILABLE: The *.domain or address range targets could not be read from the inventory, so the run was not started. Try again.
scope.error.WIDENING_NEEDS_APPROVER: Only a scope approver can widen what may be probed.
scope.error.WILDCARD_TARGET: This wildcard cannot be a scan target: write *.example.com for a domain your organization may scan (not a public suffix or a shared provider domain), in the targets rather than the scanner settings.

scope.exclusion.testingNeedsApprover: Changing how a path may be tested needs the exclusion approve permission.

scope.existing.exclusion.pending: {pattern} is already out of scope and is waiting for approval. Scans still reach it until it is approved.
scope.existing.exclusion.pendingOpen: {pattern} was put out of scope earlier and still waits for an approval your organization no longer requires. Put it in effect to use it.
scope.existing.exclusion.rejected: {pattern} was put out of scope before and rejected. Remove the rejected exclusion to add it again.
scope.existing.exclusion.unknown: {pattern} is already in the Out of scope list.

scope.intrusive.longestHint: How long an entry that allows intrusive (T2) probes may last. Every T2 entry still needs a verified domain and an approval. Long and permanent T2 entries are confirmed again periodically, or they fall back to non-intrusive (T1).
scope.intrusive.ownerHint: Only an owner changes this. Saving asks for a reason and for you to confirm your identity; it is audited and every administrator is told.

scope.list.issue.tooLong: Too long for a scope entry.
scope.list.issue.unrecognized: Not a domain, IP address, IP range, URL, repository or cloud account.

scope.review.readOnly: You can view these items. Deciding ownership needs permission to edit assets.

scope.selfApprove.description: Nobody else in your organization can approve {pattern}. As an owner you may approve it yourself. This is recorded in the audit log and every administrator is told.
scope.selfApprove.reason: Why may it take effect without a second person?
scope.selfApprove.title: Approve your own entry
scope.settings.approvalsHint: Adding or widening an entry waits for this many other approvers. With the default, your organization needs {fallback}; with this choice it needs {next}. An organization with two or more administrators never goes below one.
scope.settings.approvalsNeededHint: From {count} administrators; the requester never counts. Intrusive (T2) entries always need one.
scope.settings.approvalsNeededHintOne: From 1 administrator; the requester never counts. Intrusive (T2) entries always need one.
scope.settings.autoCoverageHint: On (default): every asset your scope covers gets the checks its type needs (DNS, ports, HTTP probe, templates) on a schedule and when it appears or changes, with no scan to set up. Scope, exclusions, windows and guardrails still decide what may be scanned; intrusive checks never run this way.
scope.settings.autoCoverageStrict: Strict scan approval is in force, so it is off until you turn it on.
scope.settings.autoJoinHint: A name discovery finds under a permanent scope entry is confirmed as yours. IP addresses are confirmed only through IP entries; one-off entries never confirm names; exclusions and names marked not yours always win. Off: such names stay discovered until a person confirms them (a scope entry still lets scans reach them).
scope.settings.checksHint: Every scan target must be covered by a scope entry, seed or verified domain. No setting turns this off.
scope.settings.ciScopeRequiresProofHint: Off (default): the repositories a CI trust names are in scope as soon as the trust is saved, and a verified pipeline run is shown as evidence. On: a CI trust's new repository entries wait until a verified pipeline run under them.
scope.settings.confirmAddsToScope: Confirming an asset adds it to scope
scope.settings.confirmAddsToScopeHint: A person who confirms a domain, subdomain or public address as yours also adds the scope entry for exactly that name, with the same re-authentication, notice and audit as adding it by hand. Addresses behind your names are never added this way. Under Strict scan approval confirming records ownership only.
scope.settings.defaultTierHint: New entries allow this unless the person adding them picks otherwise.
scope.settings.description: Who may widen what your organization probes, how many must approve, and how one-off entries and discovered names behave.
scope.settings.inEffectHint: Read-only. These follow from your settings and the platform's configuration.
scope.settings.loadFailed: The scope policy could not be loaded
scope.settings.oneOff.admins.label: Approvers only
scope.settings.oneOff.admins_and_request: A member asks for one name or address for a few days; an approver approves it.
scope.settings.oneOff.disabled.hint: Nobody adds one-off entries; every entry is permanent.
scope.settings.oneOff.disabled.label: Off
scope.settings.oneOffDaysHint: Days a one-off entry may last, 1 to 30. It stops authorizing scans the moment it expires.
scope.settings.policyEditHint: Saving asks you to confirm your identity, is audited, and notifies every administrator.
scope.settings.policyReadHint: Only scope approvers can change these.
scope.settings.proof.off.hint: Scans need a scope entry, seed or verified domain, not ownership proof.
scope.settings.proof.off.label: Not required
scope.settings.proof.platform_sensors.hi: Scans that run on the platform's shared sensors need every target under a verified domain of your organization, and intrusive (T2) probes need one on any sensor. Your own sensors need a scope entry only.
scope.settings.proof.title: Active-probe proof
scope.settings.reviewBeforeInventoryHint: Off (default): what discovery finds joins the inventory at once, and gets what Scan unclassified assets allows until a scope entry covers it. On: names outside every permanent entry wait in Suggestions for a person before they join the inventory. It never changes what may be scanned.
scope.settings.saveFailed: Could not save the scope policy.
scope.settings.scanApprovalByOwner: Set by your owner in Settings > Scan approval.
scope.settings.scanApprovalOn: On: scans are approved, not scope entries
scope.settings.scanApprovalOpenHint: Widening takes effect without a second person. Re-authentication, the deny list, audit and notifications still apply.
scope.settings.scanApprovalStrictHint: Widening waits for the approvals below; intrusive (T2) entries always need one.
scope.settings.title: Scope policy
scope.settings.unclassifiedHint.full: Assets no scope entry covers get the scan’s own intensity, still behind the platform guardrails. Exclusions and Not ours always win.
scope.settings.unclassifiedHint.low_impa: Assets no scope entry covers, and nobody excluded or marked not yours, get low-impact checks: common ports at a low rate, the home page and /.well-known/, certificate and technology fingerprinting. Platform guardrails keep shared, CDN, cloud and unknown networks and names outside your domains passive.
scope.settings.unclassifiedHint.off: Assets no scope entry covers get passive checks only, until an entry covers them.
scope.settings.unclassifiedPlatformOnly: Applies to platform sensors of the hosted service. Your own sensors scan unclassified assets in full.
scope.settings.unclassifiedStrict: Strict scan approval is in force, so this is Off for now.
scope.show.label: Show
scope.testing.hint.allowed: These paths are treated as in scope until the end date, then blocked again.
scope.testing.hint.blocked: Nothing is sent to these paths.
scope.testing.hint.read_only: Only GET and HEAD requests reach these paths, so read-only checks run.
scope.tier.hint.t0: Passive only: DNS, certificates, public sources. Nothing is sent to the target.
scope.tier.hint.t1: Safe active checks: port scans, HTTP probes, non-intrusive templates.
scope.tier.hint.t2: Intrusive tests that may change state. Needs an expiry, an approval and a verified domain.
scope.tier.tools.t2: ZAP web application scans that send attack payloads
